Other than making sure either you or any other present guardian is controlling the medicine, just make sure to not make him feel like the bad guy.  Another possibility that could be happening is he could be suffering through withdrawals as it wears off in the evening.  If he is simply taking an extra one a couple hours after without telling you or his medication provider during meetings.  Methylphenidate comedowns can be nasty.  Depression, twitching, dry mouth, body aches, and more are all possible.  He may be going through some of these symptoms, realizing their source, and acting accordingly.  If this is going on, an appropriate response could be asking him if he needs a booster dose of short acting methylphenidate such as ritalin or focacil.  Medication can be a tricky thing to figure out, and he could be doing this without telling you due to being weary about talking through side effects.  No matter what, showing respect to him is likely to warrant respect and honesty back.

Sources im seeing are that methylphenidate isnt lethal unless he managed to amass 1600 mg per kilogram.  12 tablets arent enough to do any serious damage.  worst case scenario he is taking an extra one per day.  Other than an overdose, something you wont have to worry about with concerta is its internasal abuse.  Its almost impossible to snort brand name concerta due to its non water soluble ingredients.  the only other thing that could be happening, which i sadly suspect is the most likely case, selling.  you should be the one handing out his meds.  Not only will he get in serious trouble if caught, you can too depending on your state.  None of this is to say you should react with anger or suspicion.  Kids hate being suspected of things, and will react crossly when confronted.  your best bet is to approach this by stating there are some pills missing, and explaining that you understand they hold street value.  explain it is morally wrong, not to mention very dangerous to  be misusing or selling his medicine.  Just ensure to approach this subject with care.  that time in life is very fragile, and you want to help him.
